clue.text: Prudence West is taking Benedictine

parts.note: taken as written
Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A woman called Prudence from the West is taking holy orders, or perhaps a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: Benedictine looks like the liqueur; here it is a monk, styled Dom.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence and wisdom are synonyms for sound practical judgement.

clue.text: It is thought to be almost perfect

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: Something reckoned to be very nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: Refusal to give credit?

parts.note: reads like a bank declining a loan, but means refusing to believe something

explanation.surface: A lender turning down a customer's request.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to believe it, so declining to do so is unbelief.

clue.text: Fellow having plenty of time to run a business

parts.note: a fellow is a man
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A man with time on his hands sets up a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to direct or run an enterprise.

clue.text: Meat for sale at a bargain price?

definitions.text: Meat for sale at a bargain price?

parts.words: Meat for sale at a bargain price?
parts.note: read as a cheap cut of meat, but the clue also means a cut of beef from under the ribs, and a verb for selling more cheaply than a rival

explanation.surface: A butcher's sign offering cheap meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the tenderloin cut of beef and the act of underpricing a competitor.

clue.text: Luton nil in a Tyne fixture — not aiming for a goal

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new fixed arrangement, with a football fixture in the surface

explanation.surface: Luton score nothing in a match on Tyneside, never shooting at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is an English football club and Tyne suggests Newcastle; 'fixture' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without intending it is acting without aim or purpose.

clue.text: Marriage of French betrothed in the resistance

parts.note: de is French for of
a fiance is a betrothed man

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's engagement during the wartime Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marriage' joins the two pieces; it is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance to authority.

clue.text: Drawing instrument found amongst dividers?

parts.note: a straight edge kept with compasses and dividers in a geometry set, and a monarch who follows the maxim divide and rule

explanation.surface: A geometry set holds compasses, dividers and a straight edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight edge for drawing lines, and also a sovereign who rules by dividing opponents.

clue.text: Modest just the same

definitions.meaning: natural and without airs or pretence
not changed or altered in any way

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both free of pretension and not altered by something.

clue.text: He has broken links with one foreign capital

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of links are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man has snapped his ties with a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns LINKS into LSINK, which sits between HE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland, a foreign capital to the British setter.

clue.text: It may appear in a list of powerful maritime birds

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is one bird; 'It may appear in a list of' tells us the answer is one entry among them

indicators.note: the letters are seen running inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A roll-call of mighty seabirds.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey and white seabird of the petrel family.

clue.text: Musical Moroccan pub crawler?

parts.note: a tribesman from the Rif mountains of Morocco who has done the rounds of eight drinking places, read as a phrase from music

explanation.surface: A tuneful North African out on a pub crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: A Riff is a Berber of Morocco's Rif region; one who has visited eight bars is a pub crawler, and the whole names a short repeated musical phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A short phrase of eight bars repeated in jazz or rock music is the musical sense.

clue.text: Chap works for military advantage

definitions.note: singular, while the answer is the plural of the tactical moves made to gain it

parts.note: a chap is a man
oeuvres is French for works, used in English for an artist's output

explanation.surface: A man labours to give his army the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical troop movements are made to gain an edge over an enemy.

clue.text: Duty on one type of — conveyance

parts.note: a duty is a tax levied on goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on one kind of vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab for hire is one kind of conveyance, a vehicle carrying people.

clue.text: Kiss Alec in exchange for a piece of jewellery

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle

indicators.note: the letters of Alec are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone kisses Alec and gets a jewel in return.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of beads or chain worn round the neck is an item of jewellery.

clue.text: Ties of affection

parts.note: reads as emotional bonds, but means literal decorative ribbon tied as tokens between lovers

explanation.definitionFit: These are ornamental bows exchanged as tokens between sweethearts.

clue.text: Outlook from carriage

definitions.meaning: a way of thinking or point of view
bearing or posture of the body

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mental stance and the way one holds the body.

clue.text: Paper that's bought to throw away

definitions.text: Paper that's bought to throw away

parts.words: Paper that's bought to throw away
parts.note: seems a wasteful purchase, but describes small coloured paper bits bought to be thrown over a wedding couple

explanation.surface: A complaint about buying something only to bin it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are bought specifically to be thrown at weddings.

clue.text: It is seen as an opinion

definitions.meaning: a sight or scene that one looks at
a personal belief or way of thinking

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sight before the eyes and a held opinion.

clue.text: Local argument which carries weight

parts.note: a local is a pub, which has a bar
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood dispute that is taken seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelbarrow is a small cart for carrying loads.

clue.text: It normally completes the written enquiry

definitions.text: It normally completes the written enquiry

parts.words: It normally completes the written enquiry
parts.note: describes the punctuation mark placed at the end of a written question

explanation.surface: A remark about how a written query usually ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A written question normally ends with this punctuation symbol.

clue.text: A seat to put in the sun

indicators.note: the word to is placed inside

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chair to be set out in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a backless seat.

clue.text: Forecast for fish

indicators.note: the second half of the clue's first word signals that its first half is thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather prediction for the fishing fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forecast' splits into FORE and 'cast', the anagram signal, giving ORFE.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Rum loo embellished with gilt decoration

indicators.note: to embellish is to dress up and rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange lavatory has been dressed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze used for decorating furniture.

clue.text: Old port of Labrador?

indicators.note: made out of: the letters of Labrador are the material reshaped, the question mark flagging the liberty

explanation.surface: A harbour from the Canadian region of former times, or perhaps a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Labrador suggests a place or a dog with a harbour; the question mark warns that its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the archaic nautical word for the port side of a ship.

clue.text: It was instrumental in combining rest and play

indicators.note: rest and play are combined and mixed together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something that helped bring together relaxation and fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The psaltery is an ancient stringed musical instrument, so it was literally instrumental.

clue.text: Point to Elizabeth's favourite part of old England

parts.note: W, west, is a point of the compass
the Earl of Essex was a favourite of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: Indicating Queen Elizabeth's best-loved region of historic England.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was Elizabeth I's favourite courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of south-west England.
